item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00042","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C04","C10","C22"],"selected_candidate_label":"C04","confidence":0.78,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C04 plausibly supplied a compact two-step drafting template: first add or designate a new participant, then expressly make the governing provisions applicable to that participant. The child expands this machinery to four defense-connected agencies and adds contract/date details required by its statute. C10 has similar act-extension language, while C22 similarly extends an existing regulatory regime to several named agencies, but neither matches the child's designation-plus-applicability sequence as closely as C04.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"[The named entities are] hereby designated ... as agencies of the Government included within the definition of the term \"Department\" for the purposes of Title I of the Act.","parent_excerpt":"the membership of the Air Coordinating Committee ... is hereby enlarged to include a representative of the Treasury Department","explanation":"Both first expand the set of entities participating in an existing legal or administrative regime."},{"child_excerpt":"the provisions of Title I of the Act, shall be applicable to all contracts with each agency designated in paragraph 1 of this order","parent_excerpt":"the provisions of the said order shall hereafter be applicable to the Treasury Department to the same extent as they are applicable to the participating agencies named in paragraph 1 of such order","explanation":"This is a closely parallel operative follow-through: after adding the entity, the directive makes the preexisting provisions applicable to it and ties that application back to paragraph 1."}]}
